Formulation  
Patient is a 27-year-old male experiencing acute gastroenteritis symptoms (diarrhea, cramping, nausea) likely precipitated by infectious exposure (brother also unwell). Psychological distress appears mild and related to the burden of symptoms and impact on work attendance. Supportive family environment present, though patient prefers to self-manage. No prior mental health history or current mood disorder diagnosed. Protective insight and coping strategies noted. Primary focus remains physical health stabilization with secondary attention to psychosocial impact.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Psychological distress secondary to acute gastrointestinal illness  
- Patient Goal(s): To manage distress and maintain well-being during recovery; maintain work attendance as able  
- Clinical Goal(s): Support coping strategies; monitor mood and functional impact; ensure follow-up if symptoms or distress worsen  
- Actions (Patient): Follow medical advice for physical illness; communicate any worsening symptoms or distress  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide reassurance and education; monitor symptom resolution and impact on mental well-being; consider referral if psychological distress escalates  

Secondary Problem: Mild anxiety/stress related to illness and family history  
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce anxiety related to illness and family health concerns  
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide empathic support; address any emerging anxiety symptoms; facilitate social support  
- Actions (Patient): Engage with available social supports; practice relaxation/coping strategies  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Assess mental state at follow-up; provide information on anxiety management; signpost psychological support if needed  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Gastroenteritis symptoms and management, hydration importance (Dioralyte recommendation), food guidance (clear fluids, soft diet), medication use (Paracetamol use), alcohol avoidance during illness  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent or worsening diarrhea beyond 48 hours, dehydration signs, increasing pain or fever, inability to maintain fluids  
- Coping Strategies: Encouraged self-management, maintaining hydration, pacing activities, avoiding alcohol and smoking during illness
